input.prompt:
Topic: CSCI-399: CS Undergraduate Part-time Co-op. This catalog entry has student-, instructor-, or term-specific content. Create a rigorous orientation companion that teaches the stable process, standards, planning methods, evaluation criteria, and representative examples without inventing a fixed RIT syllabus. Official catalog description: Cooperative education is a work experience designed to supplement the educational process. Students may select from a range of activities designated as cooperative education as described by their program of study. Activities are done on a part-time basis. Prerequisite: CSCI-099 or equivalent course. Typically Offered: Fall, Spring, Summer

Source excerpts:

[acm-code-of-ethics]
The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Computing professionals should avoid harm. They should be honest and trustworthy. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. They should respect privacy. They should honor confidentiality. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.

[acm-research-practice]
Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Conflicts and relevant relationships should be disclosed according to publication policy. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.

[rit-csci-399]
Cooperative education is a work experience designed to supplement the educational process. Students may select from a range of activities designated as cooperative education as described by their program of study. Activities are done on a part-time basis. Prerequisite: CSCI-099 or equivalent course. Typically Offered: Fall, Spring, Summer

beats.claim: Cooperative education is a work experience designed to supplement the educational process.
beats.example: Students complete a semester-long software development project at a local tech firm while maintaining full-time coursework.
beats.title: Introduction to Cooperative Education
beats.visualDirection: Display a split-screen graphic showing a classroom lecture on the left and a student coding in a corporate office on the right, with a central arrow labeled 'Supplementing Education'.

beats.claim: Activities are done on a part-time basis to balance academic and professional responsibilities.
beats.example: The co-op schedule allocates approximately 15 hours per week, equivalent to one full-time course credit, allowing students to attend lectures and complete assignments.
beats.title: Part-Time Structure and Scheduling
beats.visualDirection: Show a weekly timeline calendar highlighting 15 hours of co-op work distributed across weekdays, with academic classes marked separately.

beats.claim: Students must complete CSCI-099 or an equivalent course before enrolling in CSCI-399.
beats.example: A freshman student who has not yet taken an introductory programming course must take CSCI-099 in the preceding semester to qualify for the co-op program.
beats.title: Prerequisite Requirements
beats.visualDirection: Create a prerequisite flowchart showing CSCI-099 as a required gateway node before the CSCI-399 co-op course node.

beats.claim: CSCI-399 is typically offered during Fall, Spring, and Summer terms.
beats.example: Students can enroll in the co-op program during any of these three academic terms, providing flexibility to align work experience with career goals.
beats.title: Term Offerings
beats.visualDirection: List the three terms (Fall, Spring, Summer) as horizontal buttons with checkmarks, indicating availability for co-op enrollment.

beats.claim: Computing professionals must contribute to society and human well-being while avoiding harm.
beats.example: A co-op student developing a healthcare app must ensure the system does not compromise patient data privacy or cause unintended harm to users.
beats.title: Ethical Foundations in Co-op
beats.visualDirection: Display a shield icon with three sub-icons representing 'Contribute to Society', 'Avoid Harm', and 'Human Well-being'.

beats.claim: Professionals should be honest and trustworthy in their work and communications.
beats.example: When documenting co-op progress, students must accurately report completed tasks and challenges without exaggerating results or omitting critical failures.
beats.title: Honesty and Trustworthiness
beats.visualDirection: Show a checklist graphic with items like 'Accurate Reporting', 'Transparent Documentation', and 'Trustworthy Updates' next to a co-op project dashboard.

beats.claim: Professionals should be fair and take action not to discriminate in their work.
beats.example: A co-op team must ensure equitable distribution of tasks and recognition among all members, regardless of background or role.
beats.title: Fairness and Non-Discrimination
beats.visualDirection: Illustrate a balanced scale with 'Equitable Task Distribution' on one side and 'Inclusive Recognition' on the other, labeled 'Fairness in Co-op Teams'.

beats.claim: Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence and cites prior work.
beats.example: When presenting co-op findings, students must clearly separate their own contributions from existing research and provide proper citations for all referenced methods.
beats.title: Responsible Technical Communication
beats.visualDirection: Show a document template with sections labeled 'Claim', 'Evidence', 'Prior Work', and 'Contribution', demonstrating proper structure.

beats.claim: Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification.
beats.example: Co-op students must verify all data sources, accurately report limitations, and never alter results to fit a desired conclusion.
beats.title: Research Integrity and Evaluation
beats.visualDirection: Create a flowchart showing 'Data Collection' -> 'Verification' -> 'Accurate Reporting' -> 'Limitations Disclosed', with red X marks over 'Fabrication' and 'Falsification'.

beats.claim: Students must apply ethical standards and communication practices to co-op planning and evaluation.
beats.example: Before submitting a co-op project, students check that they have identified stakeholders, documented methods for reproducibility, and verified all claims against evidence.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: Display a printable checklist with boxes for 'Ethical Review Complete', 'Communication Standards Met', 'Evaluation Criteria Applied', and 'Sources Cited'.

learningObjectives: Define cooperative education as a part-time work experience that supplements the academic curriculum.
Identify the prerequisite course requirement and typical term offerings for CSCI-399.
Apply ACM ethical principles and responsible technical communication standards to co-op project planning and evaluation.
